learning_outcomes.text: Learn, understand, relate and deepen the main concepts of strength of materials.
Perform internal force diagrams and obtain the stresses and deformations derived from them.
Study cases of combined stresses, as well as Euler buckling instability.
Develop critical thinking and interpretation of the results obtained.
Apply theoretical concepts to practical situations.
Train students in problem-solving and the search for the most appropriate procedure to tackle the proposed exercise.
Acquire the fundamental concepts for the study of forces, stresses, and deformations of a deformable solid.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION TO STRENGTH OF MATERIALS: The deformable body. Mechanical properties of materials. Linear elasticity and elastic properties. Structural systems. Basic assumptions.
INTERNAL FORCE DIAGRAMS: Internal forces at the cross-section. Cross-section method. Axial force diagrams. Torque moment diagrams. Shear force and bending moment diagrams.

STRESSES AND STRAINS IN A PRISMATIC SOLID: Introduction. Stress and strains in axially loaded members. Stress and strains in torsion members. Stress and strains in bending members. Optimal cross-sections. State of stresses at a point. Mohr’s circles. Yield criteria.
COMBINED LOADING: Introduction. Non-symmetric bending. Members in combined axial and bending loading.

DEFORMATIONS OF A PRISMATIC SOLID: Deformations in axially loaded members. Deformations in torsion members. Deformations in bending members. Euler-Bernoulli elastic-beam equation. Mohr’s theorems. Thermal deformations.

STRUCTURAL STABILITY: Introduction to the concept of static equilibrium. The Euler formula for columns with pinned ends. Euler buckling of columns with general end constraints. Columns with eccentric loads. Imperfections in columns.
assessment_rules: For ordinary examination, partial written exams are liberatory if a minimum of 50% is achieved in each; otherwise, the score is not retained. A minimum of 30% (0.9 out of 3 points) is required on the mandatory final exam component to pass the subject. For extraordinary examination, scores from partial tests that met the minimum for liberation will be retained. Passed parts of the ordinary final exam will not be retained for the extraordinary exam, and the 30% minimum on the mandatory final exam still applies.
